items.reason: Pinning a tag to a SHA means asking GitHub what the tag points at right now, and this session has no network; the repository already has the machinery (scripts/actions-pin.mjs --update pins AND flips STRICT/RATCHET in the same pass) and documents the one networked run that closes it.

Added .github/constraint-map.json (38 rules, each with the fence that enforces it and a rung — blocking/reporting/partial/honour), a summary table in AGENTS.md, and test-unit/constraint-map.test.mjs which fails on a claimed fence that does not exist, a quote no longer in its source, a table/JSON mismatch, a disagreement with the contract ledger, or a check:ci stage attached to no rule.

Already covered: test-llm/adversarial/corpus.json is an injection corpus for exactly this input class (campaign names synced from Google Ads/Sklik, public Google reviews, inbound twin messages), placed in the real prompt builders by test-unit/llm-adversarial.test.mjs inside check:ci, with detection/containment/refusal rungs; test-llm/injection/corpus.json does the same for the review harness. Nothing was edited to satisfy a scanner.

Mutation testing needs a test runner: a mutation harness is only real once its survival count has been measured on a chosen directory, and this session cannot run node --test or install anything, so any config or script shipped here would be a claim rather than a practice.

Making the environment declarative means writing down the Vercel project, its env var set and the Firestore/Sklik/Google credential wiring — facts that live in the operator's dashboards, not in this worktree, and that touch CODEOWNERS law files; a plausible-looking IaC file written blind would be worse than none.

Added .github/docs-staleness.json (14 governed docs, each with the paths it is watched against and a maxAgeDays), scripts/docs-staleness.mjs which measures a doc against git as overtaken/aged, and test-unit/docs-staleness.test.mjs which blocks on a moved doc, a moved watched path or an unbudgeted runbook; the age ratchet itself is reporting-rung until someone runs --accept, per ADR-0007.

Verified signatures need a key: generating or registering a signing identity for the automation lane, adding it to the repository's allowed signers or to GitHub, and configuring the lane's secret are all outside a no-shell no-network session, and a workflow that verifies signatures nobody makes yet would be a red gate on arrival.

lessons: This repository is unusually well instrumented, so the first move on any gap should be to search for the artefact that already covers it: two of seven items here were already closed by files a keyword scan does not surface (test-llm/adversarial/corpus.json for prompt-injection fixtures, .github/contract-ledger.json for rule-to-enforcement mapping). Adding a parallel mechanism would have created two answers to the same question.

Its own ADR-0007 (a check blocks only once it passes, otherwise it reports against a ratchet) is the right shape for work done in a sandbox that cannot run the suite: ship the structural half blocking (a registry whose paths must exist), and leave the measured half reporting with the one command that arms it written down.

New gates must be wired into two meta-checks or the build goes red for a reason unrelated to the change: scripts/gate-remedy.mjs must have an entry for every check:ci stage (and CHAIN must equal the chain in order), and .github/contract-ledger.json wants a row per enforced rule. Adding a script as an npm command outside check:ci avoids both while still being runnable.
